lesson.title: Defending Decisions Under Uncertainty: handling questions and stakeholder pushback
lesson.description: This session prepares students for the final delivery banca, where they will defend their simulator and business recommendations to the partner and to the evaluation panel. The class focuses on the specific challenge of defending a decision that was made under uncertainty, where the analyst must simultaneously acknowledge the limits of the model and preserve the credibility of the recommendation. Students will study the four villains of decision-making (narrow framing, confirmation bias, short-term emotion, overconfidence) from Chip and Dan Heath's WRAP framework, with particular attention to "Attain Distance Before Deciding" and "Prepare to Be Wrong", both directly applicable to how one responds to stakeholder questions. The class also addresses the dynamics of advice-giving and advice-receiving, how to handle pushback from more powerful stakeholders, and how to reposition a recommendation without abandoning its core logic.
